title: Table Manners
summary: We talked about dining experiences and table manners in different countries, like eating a tagine in Morocco. We practised interrupting politely and checking that we understand, for example 'Did you say you ate with your hands?'. We also corrected mistakes with the past simple and question word order.

grammar.title: Past simple with finished time (not present perfect)
grammar.explain: When we say when something happened (last week, yesterday, in 2020), we use the past simple, not the present perfect. This is very common when we tell a story about a dining experience.
grammar.explain_ar: عندما نذكر وقتاً منتهياً حدث فيه الشيء (الأسبوع الماضي، أمس، عام 2020) نستخدم الماضي البسيط وليس المضارع التام. وهذا شائع جداً عندما نحكي قصة عن تجربة تناول طعام.
form: subject + past simple verb + finished time (Last week, I invited my friends to my home.)
Did + subject + base verb ...? (Did you try sushi?)
invite + someone + to + a place / an event

examples.en: Last week, I invited my friends to my home.
examples.note: Teacher's correction of 'I have invited last week in my home'.

examples.en: I was in Marrakech and I was invited out to dinner by a stranger.
examples.note: Past simple (passive) for a finished story.

examples.en: We took bread and ate using our hands.
examples.note: Past simple for actions one after another in a story.

examples.en: I have never been to Morocco.
examples.note: Present perfect is fine here because there is no finished time.

mistakes.wrong: I have invited last week in my home.
mistakes.right: Last week, I invited my friends to my home.
mistakes.why: 'Last week' is finished time, so use past simple. Also: invite someone TO a place.

mistakes.wrong: They invited us in their house.
mistakes.right: They invited us to their house.
mistakes.why: We say 'invite someone to a place'.

quiz.q: Last Friday, we ___ dinner at a Moroccan restaurant.
quiz.why: 'Last Friday' is finished time, so we use past simple.

options: I have invited my friends last week.
I invited my friends last week.
I was invite my friends last week.

quiz.q: They invited us ___ their house for lunch.
quiz.why: We say 'invite someone to a place'.
After 'did', we use the base verb.

quiz.q: I ___ to Japan, but I'd love to go.
quiz.why: No finished time and talking about life experience: present perfect.

grammar.title: Question word order for checking information
grammar.explain: In questions, the verb 'be' or the helping verb (did, do) comes before the subject. 'It was spicy or sweet?' is wrong; we say 'Was it spicy or sweet?'. We use questions like 'Did you say...?' and 'What do you mean by...?' to check we understand.
grammar.explain_ar: في الأسئلة يأتي فعل «be» أو الفعل المساعد (did, do) قبل الفاعل. فلا نقول «It was spicy or sweet?» بل «Was it spicy or sweet?». ونستخدم أسئلة مثل «Did you say...?» و«What do you mean by...?» للتأكد من أننا فهمنا الكلام.
form: Was / Were + subject + ...? (Was it spicy or sweet?)
Did + subject + base verb ...? (Did you eat with your hands?)
Did you say (that) + clause? (Did you say you tried sushi?)
What do you mean by + word? (What do you mean by tagine?)
Rising intonation at the end of yes/no checking questions

examples.note: Teacher's correction of 'It was spicy or sweet?'.

examples.note: Checking something you heard; the voice goes up at the end.

examples.en: What do you mean by tagine?
examples.note: Asking about a word you don't know.

examples.en: Did you say you ate with your hands?

mistakes.why: In questions, 'was' comes before the subject 'it'.

mistakes.right: What do you mean by tagine?

mistakes.wrong: Did you said you ate with your hands?
mistakes.right: Did you say you ate with your hands?
Where did you have the meal?
mistakes.why: Past simple questions need 'did' + base verb.

quiz.why: After 'do you', use the base verb 'mean'.

quiz.why: 'The food' is singular and the main verb is 'be', so 'Was'.
Past simple question with a main verb (eat): 'did' + base verb.

quiz.q: In 'Did you say you ate with your hands?', your voice usually ___ at the end.
quiz.why: Yes/no checking questions usually have rising intonation.
